subject: Northpoint benchmarks & rate-match request (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)
messages:
From: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@northpoint.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northpoint.ai
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: can Redwood match OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS on hosted rates?

Hi Hannah,

We’re running a procurement sprint to consolidate hosted LLM spend across our data products. For a quick go/no-go we need a baseline comparison and a best-effort price check versus the vendors below for hosted API (inference + embeddings):

- OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini / embeddings)
- Anthropic (Claude Instant / embed-2)
- Together (RedPajama / inference variants)
- AWS Bedrock (Aurora-style endpoints)

For context: expected monthly usage is ~300M input tokens + 200M output tokens, plus ~5M embeddings requests. Latency SLO target: p95 <= 300ms for short prompt paths.

Can Redwood provide:
- A simple per-unit baseline rate (per 1k tokens for gen; per 1k tokens for embeddings) you can commit to match if we move 12-month reserved capacity?
- Any tiered commit discounts or blended pooling options?
- Notes on latency SLOs and whether you can route to lower-cost model variants if we accept graceful degradation?

If possible, please include a one-page comparison vs the four vendors above and any quick caveats (e.g., quantization impacts, exact model family mismatches). We’re trying to finalize preferred vendors by EOD next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Procurement Lead, Northpoint Analytics
Attachments: northpoint-competitive-ratecards.pdf (pdf stub)

----

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@northpoint.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: can Redwood match OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS on hosted rates?

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the clear brief 1 — useful. Quick answers up front, then we’ll follow with a one-page comparison and a draft ratecard.

High-level:
- Yes, we can propose a rate-match posture against the vendors you listed for a 12-month committed volume.
- We offer blended committed tiers (monthly committed token pool across gen + embeddings) or line-item commits if you prefer separation.
- Latency: for short prompt paths we can commit to p95 <= 300ms on our dedicated pool in the US with an agreed uptime SLA; hosted API best-effort latency is similar in practice but we recommend Dedicated for strict SLOs.

What I’m attaching: a draft Redwood ratecard (redwood-draft-ratecard-05042028.pdf) and a short competitive notes doc. The draft includes:
- Per-1k token baseline for generation (standard models) and a separate embeddings unit price.
- Commit tiers: 0-50M, 50-300M, 300M+ token buckets with step-up discounts.
- A suggested "fallback variant" policy: if capacity constrained we can route to a quantized variant explicitly listed (we flag expected quality delta).

Two quick clarifying asks so we align the benchmark:
1) Do your numbers treat input+output tokens together for billing or separately? (We price per input/output token individually but can present a blended view.)
2) For embeddings, are you measuring by request count or by token-equivalent? (OpenAI often bills embeddings per request; we can align the comparison however you prefer.)

If you want me + Marissa to jump on a 30-min call early next week we can walk the comparison and firm the offer.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0184
Attachments: redwood-draft-ratecard-05042028.pdf (pdf stub); competitive-notes-05042028.txt (text stub)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@northpoint.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick: can Redwood match OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS on hosted rates?

Looping in a quick internal playbook and initial price levers we can offer to match/beat comps. Sarah 1 feel free to skip to the bolded bullets and call out must-haves.

Playbook (internal -> shared):
- Anchor: ask for three-month billing history or expected token mix; commit pricing should be scoped to blended token pricing (gen + embeddings).
- Pricing levers we can use (examples for 12-month commit):
  * 0-299M blended tokens/month: baseline - $X.XX per 1k gen tokens; embeddings $Y.YY per 1k
  * 300-999M: baseline - ~15% off baseline
  * 1B+: best-in-class panel pricing, custom pool + dedicated capacity (additional discount, SLA)
- One-off credits: onboarding credit to offset first-month peak usage if procurement requests calendar alignment.
- Technical concessions: priority queueing on dedicated pool, consult hours to optimize prompt/quantization, extended log retention for 90 days (audit-friendly).

Operational notes to share with procurement:
- We’ll provide a short perf-run (your test corpus) on our hosted API and on a dedicated pool so you can compare latency profiles side-by-side.
- Fallback policy: documented model variants + expected quality delta; optional canary and A/B routes during rollout.

For the external doc we should propose the following simple packaging options:
- Option A (Hybrid Hosted): 12-month committed blended pool, small monthly commit, credits for first month, standard support.
- Option B (Dedicated SLO): 12-month reserved capacity + enhanced SLA, priority routing, lower per-token rate at 300M+ commitment.
- Option C (Pilot): 3-month pilot with pilot discount + performance credits, then convert to A or B.

Hannah: can you fold these bullets into the one-pager and mark a recommended option? I’d lean Marissa to propose Option B for Northpoint given their p95 constraint and token volume.

-Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Hannah and Vivek 1 that was fast and very helpful. A few quick follow-ups:

- We bill gen input+output separately; please include both views (separate and blended).
- For embeddings, we use per-request accounting (not tokens) 1 please include a per-request rate.
- We’d like Option B as the recommended path but ask you to also include a tight pilot plan (Option C) to validate latency on our real traffic for 30 days before we flip the 12-month commitment.

Can you send the one-pager and the draft contract language (standard SOW + SLA callouts) by COB Monday? Procurement will use that to finalize shortlist.

Appreciate it,
Sarah
